title: Deprecation / Update Policy for onnx dependencies / Release Process?
body:
Hello,

since Onnx has developed into a quasi-standard in some areas, I think it could makes sense
to write down how Onnx relates to other projects and what dependencies there are. 

I want to avoid the expression _best practices_ and would therefore call it _good practices_ or _guidelines_.
When do we update/upgrade dependencies for e.g. _python_, _numpy_, _pybind_, _protobuf_ (and increase the version in requirements-min.txt?

For python versions, for example, I had the impression (I haven't checked now) that we will remove at EOL with the next ONNX release?

Could something like this be interesting for us or are we somehow oriented in this direction? 
https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/

I don't want to introduce a new formal system, I just want to understand the current practice and I think it would make sense to write this down.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Examples where guidelines would be helpful / informative? https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/6330 and https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/6167

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: About the broader question (general guidance): I think it should be driven by the needs of the community that uses onnx: including onnxruntime, pytorch, etc. and users of those as well. Eg., if pytorch or onnxruntime support a (python or whatever) version, we may need to support it. Conversely, if they drop support for some version, we can also do so.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Further context: onnxruntime dropped Python 3.8 and 3.9 support in 1.20.0: https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/tag/v1.20.0

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
My suggestion would be something like this: “As a general rule, we remove python versions about 6 months after end of life. Contact us if you would like to have a version before that, or if you want to postpone the deprecation time a little”

Since I don't expect an Onnx release in the near future, my suggestion would be to delete 3.8 support and include a sentence as mentioned in the doc.

comments.author: reporter
participant1
comments.body: Thanks. I personally don't have a concern. I would invite more people to chime in.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I think the are a couple of things conflated in this issue:
- When and how are dependencies updated
- What should the release cadence be

I have a few thoughts on each point:

> When and how are dependencies updated

https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/ seems like a good guideline to follow for Python dependencies. I don't think there is a need to support Python versions after their EOL. Some dependencies like Protobuf may require some special attention, though. One thing to note might be that we aim to depend on explicit releases rather than an unreleased commit.

> What should the release cadence be

I think a high cadence (e.g. ever 6-8 weeks) of SemVer compatible  releases would be ideal. This means that bug fixes quickly make it to the user and there is no pressure on getting individual PRs into a looming PR.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
1. It would be nice if we can follow https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/. My hesitation is that ONNX is an important dependency for PyTorch which supports a wider range of Python versions. To support PyTorch there may be a need to support more Python versions. (E.g. PyTorch still supports 3.9)
2. Having bug fixes frequently may be ideal, but it does mean a higher maintenance cost that needs to be shared by the community. Streamlining the release process, which @reporter  has made significant contributions on, would definitely help.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> 1. It would be nice if we can follow https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/. My hesitation is that ONNX is an important dependency for PyTorch which supports a wider range of Python versions. To support PyTorch there may be a need to support more Python versions. (E.g. PyTorch still supports 3.9)

Just for my understanding: to what extent is this truly a hard requirement? The PyPI version of PyTorch does not explicitly depend on onnx. Is it an explicit goal of this project to be more conservative than PyTorch?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The torch.onnx component is dependent on onnx so onnx is needed when users what to export models from PyTorch. We need the latest version of onnx to have access to the latest proto definitions

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> > 1. It would be nice if we can follow https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/. My hesitation is that ONNX is an important dependency for PyTorch which supports a wider range of Python versions. To support PyTorch there may be a need to support more Python versions. (E.g. PyTorch still supports 3.9)
> 
> Just for my understanding: to what extent is this truly a hard requirement? The PyPI version of PyTorch does not explicitly depend on onnx. Is it an explicit goal of this project to be more conservative than PyTorch?

From my point of view, it also depends on the type of dependency. I would be very conservative with the Python version, although EOL as the end of the line sounds sensible to me, but I don't think it's necessary to end support even earlier. 

For me, Pytorch would not be the reference for when to discontinue something, but as I wrote, I really appreciate their transparency with regard to discontinuations and upgrades. 

My preference would be for us to be “significantly” more conservative than community tools based on them, as we also want to run in industrial environments, for example, which are more difficult to update and where every change in the framework conditions has to be scrutinized more critically.

comments.body: I added a first version at https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/RELEASE-MANAGEMENT.md and would close the issue now. For additional comments feel free to comment or open the issue again.
